article_text:
ゴッホ、モネ、ルノワールの名画がコスメに。ボビイ ブラウンとメトロポリタン美術館が限定コラボ

ボビイ ブラウンと メトロポリタン美術館 がコラボレーションした限定コレクションが、11月12日に発売された。 ゴッホ の《糸杉のある麦畑》やモネの《睡蓮の池にかかる橋》など、美術館が所蔵する名画をメイクアップ製品やスキンケアアイテムのパッケージに採用している。

コスメブランドのボビイ ブラウン（BOBBI BROWN）が、 ニューヨーク の メトロポリタン美術館（The Met） とコラボレーションした2026年ホリデーコレクションを発売した。

メトロポリタン美術館のヨーロッパ絵画部門には、13世紀から20世紀初頭にかけての2500点以上の作品が収蔵されている。今回のコラボレーションでは、その膨大なコレクションから色彩や装飾性に特徴のある作品が選ばれ、 フィンセント・ファン・ゴッホ 、 クロード・モネ 、 ピエール＝オーギュスト・ルノワール 、アンリ＝エドモン・クロス、 オディロン・ルドン らの作品が、アイシャドウやリップ、ファンデーションなどのパッケージへと生まれ変わった。

なかでも注目したいのが、ゴッホの《糸杉のある麦畑》（1889年）を取り入れた「ザ メット アイシャドウ パレット」（税込1万1000円）だ。ゴッホが南仏サン＝レミの療養院に滞在していた時期に描いた同作は、風に揺れる麦畑と空へ伸びる糸杉、うねるような雲を、力強い筆触によって表現した風景画。ゴッホ自身も、この作品を1889年夏の優れた成果のひとつと考えていたという。

今回のパレットには、ゴッホの色彩に着想を得た8色を収録。ピンクやモーヴ、ライラック、ラベンダーに加え、日常使いしやすいニュートラルカラーを組み合わせた。コンパクトには絵画のディテールが額装を思わせるデザインであしらわれ、絵画を持ち歩くような感覚を演出する。

一方、クロード・モネの《睡蓮の池にかかる橋》（1899年）は、「ウェイトレス スキン クッション ファンデーション SPF40（PA+++）」（税込8690円）の限定コンパクトに採用された。モネは1893年、フランス・ジヴェルニーの自宅近くに土地を購入し、睡蓮の池や日本風の橋を備えた水の庭を造営した。1899年には池に架かる橋を主題とした連作に取り組み、光や水面の反射によって変化する風景を描いた。今回のコンパクトでは、緑に包まれた橋と水面の色彩が円形のケースを彩っている。

また、ルノワールの《海辺にて》（1883年）は、人気のクレンジングオイル「スージング クレンジング オイル」（400mL、税込1万3200円）の限定ボトルに登場。同作は、ルノワールがノルマンディー海岸の習作をもとに、アトリエで描いたと考えられている作品だ。丁寧に描写された女性の顔立ちと、自由な筆触による海岸風景との対比が特徴で、印象派の表現から新たな人物画の様式へと向かう時期のルノワールの関心がうかがえる。

さらに、ゴッホが1890年に描いた《アイリス》は、「シアーフィニッシュ プレストパウダー」（税込7700円）のコンパクトに採用。サン＝レミの療養院を退院する直前に描かれた同作は、花瓶に生けられた紫色のアイリスと淡い背景の色彩が印象的な静物画だ。

アンリ＝エドモン・クロスの《「コーク・オークスの下」の習作》（1908年頃）は、リップカラー「エクストラ カラー シャイン」（税込5060円）の限定ケースに。クロスは新印象派の画家として知られ、細かな色彩の筆触を重ねることで光の効果を追求した。今回採用された作品にも、鮮やかな色彩を重ねる独自の表現が見られる。

また、象徴主義の画家オディロン・ルドンによる《花束》（1900〜1905年頃）は、チークとリップの両方に使用できる「ポット ルージュ ベルベット マット」（税込5830円）のパッケージを飾る。幻想的なイメージで知られるルドンが晩年に取り組んだ花の静物画は、豊かな色彩と想像力に満ちた作品として知られている。

制作に携わったボビイ ブラウンのグローバル・プロ・アーティスト、カサンドラ・ガルシアは、同館のヨーロッパ絵画コレクションから着想を得て、ロマンティック、クラシック、モダンという3つのメイクアップスタイルを提案している。

The legal challenges to Donald Trump ’s proposed memorial arch are mounting, with the District of Columbia and Virginia suing in federal court on Saturday as the administration says construction could begin as early as next week.

There are now three lawsuits calling for a halt to potential work on a monument that would rise 250ft (76 meters) on a patch of grass off the bridge that spans the Potomac River, connecting the city with the Arlington national cemetery. That would make the arch 100ft taller (30 meters) than the Statue of Liberty is from its base to the top of the torch.

The US district judge Tanya Chutkan is already considering issuing an order to halt the project until the original lawsuit against the Trump administration by three Vietnam war veterans and an architectural historian is resolved. She held a hearing on Friday but did not immediately act, though she said she would move expeditiously.

In the latest lawsuit, two attorneys general, Brian Schwalb of Washington DC and Jay Jones of Virginia, argue that “as soon as defendants break ground on this project, they will inflict irreparable harm on both the District and Virginia. The arch site sits at the center of a major traffic artery between the District and Virginia, in the monumental core of the capital, on an island that straddles the Potomac River. During the three-year period of construction, the arch project will inevitably snarl traffic between the jurisdictions, produce pollution and storm water runoff in the Potomac, interfere with emergency services, and pose numerous other challenges.”

As the original plaintiffs have, they also are seeking a temporary restraining order that would slow the administration’s plans to move ahead imminently with construction.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The lawsuit raises concerns about how the traffic interruption would affect emergency responses in a region where joint operations are the norm, and where a January 2025 midair collision between a US military helicopter and passenger airliner killed 67 people.

The Republican administration, in a recent court filing, said it had plans to seek final approval of the project, a Trump favorite, at Thursday’s meeting of the Capital National Planning Commission and possibly begin construction the same day, despite the two pending lawsuits.

On Friday, the government submitted a 106-page plan for the arch that envisions a massive structure more than 12 stories high that includes a huge bronze statue of Lady Liberty with wings and carrying a torch with an eternal flame. The structure would include an observation deck with views to the east and west, an “occupied roof” and two mezzanines.

Inside the arch are rooms for program space, offices, a staff lounge, circular staircases, multiple elevators and a “fire command center”. The project proposes significant traffic changes in the area, including rerouting traffic on nearby roads. Administration officials have said the arch also will have a national security function.

article_text:
One day after the historic rout by the Democrats nationwide on Election Day a week ago, Trump took to the construction site of the sprawling ballroom he is constructing on the grave of the East Wing of the White House, which he abruptly razed in October 2025. “Trump invited reporters into a cavernous construction site and talked about the building project for nearly 20 minutes,” reported PBS , “without mentioning sweeping Republican defeats around the country the night before.”

The next day, Solicitor General D. John Sauer filed a petition asking the Supreme Court to greenlight the 90,000-square-foot construction project, including the 22,000-square-foot ballroom-cum-military complex. He asked the justices to rule on whether a district court, at the behest of the National Trust for Historic Preservation, erred in August in enjoining the ongoing “renovation” of the East Wing. The $400 million project has been the subject of heated debate and lawsuits since its inception. Sauer asks that the court reverse a lower court’s ruling outright or hear oral arguments, explains SCOTUSblog .

The petition starts off by claiming the injunction was granted “at the behest of a single passerby claiming she will dislike how the new building looks.” That passerby was Alison K. Hoagland, a member of the board of the National Trust for Historic Preservation. The question of whether she has legal standing to sue is a central issue in the ongoing argument.

Sauer claims she has no standing, because the court has ruled that “mere offense, disagreement, or distaste does not qualify as a concrete and particularized injury.” He further calls the ballroom a “vital national-security effort taking place on the White House grounds with the President’s personal involvement,” arguing that it is necessary because the president faces “an onslaught of assassination attempts.” (There have been, counting generously, three.)

A consultation with the Secret Service and the National Parks Service, says the petition, determined that demolition and rebuilding would be the most cost-effective course of action and would be best “to ensure that the East Wing remains minimally visible from public spaces.”

The old structure couldn’t support the ballroom’s necessary security features, says the White House, including blast-proof windows, fortified walls, and missile-resistant columns. Nor could the underground military installation be built under the existing structure.

In April 2026, US District Court judge Richard J. Leon wrote a searing 35-page opinion, employing some 18 exclamation marks , rejecting Trump’s plan for the ballroom, saying that “the President of the United States is the steward of the White House for future generations of First Familes. He is not, however, the owner!”

The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia froze Leon’s order to allow the court time to consider the government’s appeal, outlines SCOTUSblog. A three-judge panel upheld Leon’s ruling in August but pushed its effective date back two weeks to allow the federal government to go to the Supreme Court. The majority wrote that only Congress has the power “to regulate the construction and demolition of White House structures.” A dissenting judge said Hoagland had no standing.

The Trump administration called Leon’s ruling “extraordinary and unlawful,” and Sauer asked the justices to pause the ruling, saying construction was “vitally required by national security” and that Hoagland’s “dislike” for the new construction doesn’t constitute a legal injury.

In August, a federal court ruled that Trump lacked the authority to build without Congressional approval, but the Supreme Court greenlighted the construction project in a stay issued by Chief Justice John Roberts; the Court ruled 5–4 for the White House on August 31. Roberts dissented and, along with Ketanji Brown Jackson, Elena Kagan, and Sonia Sotomayor, ruled that the construction “is likely unlawful” and that the majority decision was “no victory for the separation of powers” and that Hoagland did have standing.

In any event, there’s no turning back now, says Sauer, writing that the project is 70% complete, “and, in turn ( sic ), there remains no sound way now to redesign or unwind the massive superstructure that is currently standing at the White House.”

Introduction

After 17 years of marriage, the seemingly stable lives of an acclaimed architect and his publisher wife begin to unravel when he accepts a controversial commission to build a luxury bunker for a tech billionaire. With an impeccable sense of atmosphere and pacing, this intense character study from the writer-director of The Son (LFF 2022) and The Father evolves into an unsettling moral puzzle where desire, privilege and paranoia collide.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

How to book

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.

Possible Love

Lee Chang-dong’s masterfully directed follow-up to Burning (LFF 2018) finds four strangers’ lives entwined by hidden desires and repressed emotions.

A genre-defying queer epic, rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, this is majestic and original filmmaking.

article_text:
Barbara Barrie , a character actress best known for playing boisterous moms in “ Breaking Away ” and “ Private Benjamin ,” has died. She was 95.

Barrie’s daughter, Jane Harnick, told the New York Times that her mother had terminal cancer and said her death was “medically assisted.”

Barrie was an inveterate scene stealer who was a frequent presence on stage and screen. On Broadway, she appeared in the original cast of Stephen Sondheim’s “Company,” a revolutionary musical that examined relationships and commitment. Barrie earned a Tony Award nomination for her role in the 1970 production. Other Broadway credits included Neil Simon’s hit “California Suite.”

For her film work, Barrie won the best actress prize at the 1964 Cannes Film Festival for “One Potato, Two Potato,” an interracial romance, in which her character confronts prejudice while falling in love with a Black man. But it was “Breaking Away,” and her work as the blue-collar mother of a cycling enthusiast, that put Barrie on the map. She was nominated for best supporting sctress for the 1979 coming-of-age classic, then reprised the part in a 1980 TV series based on “Breaking Away,” earning an Emmy nomination.

Barrie also was known to audiences for her turn on the 1970s detective sitcom “ Barney Miller ,” portraying the wife of the title character. Other credits included the films “Judy Berlin,” “The Bell Jar,” and Disney’s “Hercules,” as well as appearances on “Law & Order” and “Suddenly Susan.”

Barrie was a published author. She wrote children’s books, as well as “Second Act” and “Don’t Die of Embarrassment,” which examined her battle with colorectal cancer.

Taking the familiar blue and gold tropes that represent the European Union, the German-born photographer explores the visuality of the complex constructs of the Commission with his project A Circle of 12 Gold Stars on a Blue Background

Depictions of the European Union are often limited to a handful of recurring themes – close-ups of European Commission leaders on podiums, renderings of glass-heavy institutional building facades, obsessive picturings of the Union’s waving blue flag. Jan Staiger is attempting to photograph the bureaucratic machinery of the EU with the same image conventions, his project A Circle of 12 Gold Stars on a Blue Background restaging the Union’s determined types, while flipping its visual language.

Created across four European countries – Belgium, Germany, France and Greece – A Circle of 12 Gold Stars on a Blue Background traces the tropes of EU political communication. Idealised self-images and self-picturings, these representations are often far from the realities of the place. “I see the European district in Brussels as a sort of imaginary political green screen,” says Staiger, who was born in the German city Nuremberg, but is now based in Brussels, where the EU has its headquarters. “If you walk 20 minutes further, you see all the issues European capitals face displayed on the street.”

“I see the European district in Brussels as a sort of imaginary political green screen” – Jan Staiger

Staiger’s photographic record is constrained, partly through necessity. While working in European Commission buildings, photographers are watched by press officers, he says, adding, “you’re never alone”. They are also forced to follow the Commission’s protocols as laid out in its Visual Identity Manual. Staiger turns these protocols against themselves, his images made ghostly by sharp artificial light, the staged EU regalia emptied of its performative energy.

In one striking shot, 10 blue balloons – each printed with the ring of 12 gold stars – bob in the rough waters off Lesbos, Greece. The island has been central to EU migration policy since 2015, when it became an arrival point for hundreds of thousands crossing from Turkey. Staiger’s balloons read as iconographic buoys, EU symbolism set adrift within the migration crisis its politics have yet to resolve.

Staiger began A Circle of 12 Gold Stars on a Blue Background during his MA studies at KASK School of Arts in Ghent, and the series perhaps takes its most concentrated form in his book of the same name. Designed around the European Commission Visual Identity Manual , it is bound like an official document stack, and carries the title in all 24 official EU languages. The publication’s laser-cut cover references an overlooked alternative design for the European flag, stars scattered in the member states’ rough geographical positions, not the neat, equalising circle there is today.

This alternative flag hints at Staiger’s hopes for the EU and its visual representation, which is for reform not complete overhaul. “I’m not naive,” he says. “I cannot change an entire media landscape.”

Angel Studios is introducing a broad new content policy that bans on-screen sex, nudity, F-words and misusing the name of God. The studio, known for films such as the hit “Sound of Freedom,” will also give its paying members a chance to vote on movies and TV shows to ensure that a majority of members approve of the content.

Angel’s co-founder and chief content officer Jeff Harmon announced “The Angel Promise” in a Fox News interview Thursday, explaining why the studio is taking the strong approach. “I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble. These are excellent craftsmen. They’re the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world. But at the same time, they’ve kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve.”

The new policy introduces three commitments from Angel regarding audience approval of content, strict standards for sex and language and expanded parental controls.

“We promise there’s never going to be nudity, and there’ll never be sex on screen,” Harmon said in the video, explaining that Angel is a “faith-friendly studio.”

“No sex acts on screen — ever” reads the pledge on the Angel Studios website , “No F words. And no profanity in titles submitted for young kids (12 and under). Angel will not release original films or series that misuse God’s name.”

Harmon says the Angel Guild numbers approximately 3 million paying members. The new policy requires that films and television series receive a score of at least 70 out of 100 from members to be included in Angel’s programming.

“This is the first time in history that a major Hollywood studio, or top 10 studio in the United States, has come and said, we’re going to let the audience have a veto right,” Harmon told Fox.

Angel Studios releases include “Runner, “Young Washington” and “David.” Upcoming titles include “Drummer Boy,” “Angel and the Badman” and “Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ.”

article_text:
Sem complicar uma premissa que funciona justamente pela simplicidade, David Robert Mitchell leva sua experiência com o terror para um blockbuster com cara de aventura oitentista.

“ O Fim da Rua ” encontra uma premissa de ficção científica gigantesca no lugar mais banal possível. Não se trata apenas de um bairro residencial comum com pequenos conflitos familiares que parecem enormes até o momento em que deixam de ser. É aquele subúrbio americano que qualquer fã de filmes dos anos 1980 e 1990 se acostumou a reconhecer como o começo de uma aventura divertida. Até que, durante uma noite aparentemente qualquer, uma luz atravessa as janelas e um estrondo interrompe o silêncio. Pela manhã, Denise (Anne Hathaway), Greg (Ewan McGregor) e os filhos Audrey (Maisy Stella) e Brian (Christian Convery) descobrem que o bairro inteiro foi deslocado para o período jurássico.

David Robert Mitchell entende que não precisa complicar muito essa ideia. Não há qualquer necessidade de mitologia extensa ou explicações demais, apenas a reação de pessoas comuns ao perceber que o mundinho conhecido do outro lado da porta se tornou completamente hostil. Os personagens não se tornam especialistas em sobrevivência assim que os dinossauros aparecem. Eles erram disparos, tomam decisões ruins, discutem quando deveriam permanecer em silêncio e demoram a compreender as regras da situação. Mitchell extrai humor e tensão justamente dessa falta de preparo, mantendo a aventura próxima de pessoas que improvisam por puro instinto de sobrevivência.

O diretor opta por não exibir imediatamente sua principal atração e gasta um tempo considerável desenvolvendo o dia a dia dos personagens, tendo em vista a curta duração. O longa constrói a presença dos dinossauros por meio de ruídos e movimentos fora de quadro, dando sinais de que alguma coisa invadiu a rotina suburbana. Há algo da lógica de “E.T. – O Extraterrestre” nessa aproximação gradual com o desconhecido, embora a influência do cinema produzido por Steven Spielberg e pela Amblin durante os anos 1980 esteja em toda parte.

Mitchell, porém, não se limita a reproduzir essa estética de blockbuster clássico. Isso fica visível principalmente na violência surpreendente para um filme PG-13, tanto pela exposição gráfica quanto pelas consequências mais explícitas. As criaturas não se contém; quando atacam, há sangue, corpos e mortes que rompem deliberadamente com a segurança associada à aventura familiar. Nem mesmo o bom humor corriqueiro elimina esse peso, e a ameaça dos dinossauros não soa inofensiva. O cineasta se mostra à vontade em testar os limites de uma produção voltada a um público geral.

A vizinhança, mesmo parecendo um bairro comum, torna-se um labirinto, de modo que uma simples travessia entre casas adquire a dimensão de uma perseguição. O diretor utiliza planos mais longos que percorrem garagens, janelas, árvores e fundos de casas, sempre deixando escancarada a possibilidade de surgimento de um novo monstro. Essa abordagem ajuda a compensar efeitos visuais que nem sempre mantêm o mesmo nível, com algumas criaturas se integrando melhor aos ambientes do que outras. Ainda assim, “O Fim da Rua” raramente depende apenas da qualidade de um modelo digital para funcionar. Som, enquadramento, montagem e reação dos atores são mais que suficientes para construir o clima de ameaça antes mesmo de algum dinossauro ocupar a tela.

Anne Hathaway é fundamental nesse processo. Sua personagem poderia se resumir apenas à figura da mãe encarregada de proteger os filhos, mas a atriz transparece as contradições de uma mulher que já estava à beira de uma ruptura antes dos acontecimentos. Os problemas conjugais não somem, mas são somados à ameaça externa. Já Ewan McGregor constrói um Greg mais contido, favorecendo a dinâmica entre os dois. A química do casal se destaca na familiaridade de duas pessoas que compartilham uma vida muito anterior àquela crise.

Há um frescor cativante na modéstia do longa, que em nenhum momento se constrange por ser não mais que uma aventura sobre uma família cercada por dinossauros. Em apenas cem minutos, o longa apresenta os personagens, estabelece o fenômeno, constrói suas regras e acelera progressivamente até um último ato voltado à sobrevivência, quando Mitchell abandona de vez a contenção inicial e coloca os monstros no centro da aventura. Algumas ideias exigem certa disposição para aceitar a lógica proposta, mas o roteiro felizmente evita interromper a aventura com explicações excessivas, e o ritmo ganha força depois de um primeiro ato mais moroso.

“O Fim da Rua” funciona porque reconhece exatamente o tamanho de sua proposta. Mitchell entrega um filme que encontra personalidade dentro de referências muito claras ao recuperar o espírito da aventura familiar dos anos 1980 sem eliminar sua própria inclinação para o suspense e para uma violência mais suja. É como voltar ao subúrbio das aventuras de Spielberg e da Amblin , mas descobrir que, desta vez, os dinossauros realmente podem comer alguém.

article_text:
Zendaya is dusting off her “Dune” boots and getting back into the world of science fiction.

The star has boarded a new untitled sci-fi to be written and directed Alex Garland for A24 . Plot details are being kept under wraps, but the feature is set to shoot in 2027.

The project marks the latest collaboration between Zendaya and A24 following hit series “Euphoria,” which concluded after three seasons earlier this year, and the pitch-black dramedy “The Drama” alongside Robert Pattinson, which became a box office hit, earning almost $135 million worldwide.

For Garland, the film continues his long-running collaboration with A24, which has produced and distributed his 2024 sci-fi “Ex Machina,” plus “Civil War,” “Men” and “Warfare.” A24 is also behind his upcoming big-budget “Elden Ring” video game adaptation, starring Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, Ben Whishaw, Nick Offerman and Tom Burke. Shooting on “The Elden Ring” wrapped on July 30, with the film set to be released in March 2028.

Alongside “The Drama,” Zendaya has appeared in two of 2026’s biggest movies in “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which both smashed box office records. Denis Villeneuve’s final trip to Arrakis, “Dune: Part Three” releases Dec. 16.

Fans of Garland’s sci-fi — which also includes Netflix feature “Annihilation” and the FX series “Devs” — may be delighted to hear he’s returning to the genre. But the news could also dent hopes for a third “28 Years Later.” Garland wrote “28 Days Later,” later reuniting with Danny Boyle for last year’s “28 Years Later” and its quick-fire sequel “28 Years Later: The Bone Temple.” Speaking recently at the London Film Festival, Boyle said Garland had written a “fantastic script” for the third “28 Years Later” but noted he was now busy working on “Elden Ring.” “So it’s on the back burner at the moment,” he said.

Garland’s new sci-fi may push it even further back.

‘Approaching desire with curiosity’: the many facets of Black masculinity – in pictures

Through thoughtful conversations and dynamic images, Quil Lemons’s new book Quiladelphia explores how Black men navigate desire and masculinity as well as the stereotypes placed on them. With a foreword by Brontez Purnell and including Lemons in dialogue with musician Santigold and artist Lyle Ashton Harris, Lemons asks the audience to consider who can embody the American dream

Lifelong Democratic Party supporter Michael Douglas has said he is hoping for an electoral “massacre” in the upcoming U.S. midterm elections in which support for Donald Trump will be decimated.

“I’m hoping for a massacre, and we’ll see … overwhelming Democratic votes across the board,” the Wall Street and Basic Instinct star said in an interview with the BBC’s Today program on Wednesday, while in the UK to promote his autobiography One Helluva Ride .

Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President

“The president has exhausted his promises and repetitions, and we’re seeing areas, especially in the Midwest, that haven’t been Democratic in years,” he said.

“Obviously, Congress is going to change and I think — it wasn’t thought possible until recently – that the Senate will too.”

Watch on Deadline

Douglas also addressed Democrats’ plans to reactivate investigations into accusations of corruption and cronyism against Trump and his political allies.

RELATED: CNN’s Scott Jennings Hit With $72.5M Suit By Hasan Piker Over “Manipulated” Lynching Misquote

Until now, requests for documents and testimony have gone ignored. Control of the Congress would give the Democrats power to issue subpoenas for this information.

He suggested that the Democrats would tackle the cost-of-living crisis first but ultimately would turn their attention to the accusations, without directly targeting Trump.

“They’ve got a pretty good plan as to what they want to do, and it doesn’t mean indicting the president immediately,” he said. “I think they hear the people talk, and they’re going to work on these issues of affordability, if there is this dramatic change.

RELATED: Donald Trump Says He’ll Ban The Use Of The Term “Artificial Intelligence” In “All Relevant Documents” And “Everything Else”

“Then, I think they’re going to start handpicking the people around Trump — the people that made a lot of money. … There’s a lot of corruption issues, and they’re going to start to one-by-one pick them off.”

The two-time Oscar winner, who is a longtime Democrat donor, was asked whether he was “worried” about the way his support and that of other Hollywood stars had been used by Trump to suggest the party was one of elites and out of touch.

RELATED: CNN, MS NOW And Politico Amend Lawsuit To Challenge Trump Ban On Access To Air Force One And The Oval Office

“I haven’t really felt that because the reason that he achieves such a degree of success was that he was a major television star on The Apprentice … 12 years he was, like, a leading star,” he said.

“Everybody knew him, and it reflected exactly into his image as the president. ‘You’re fired, I’m the boss’, and that’s why people loved him. Yeah, we’re a liberal-bent party, and people like Bobby De Niro and some others have no problem telling him how he feels. But I haven’t felt that personal attack, no.”

「関西文化の日」とは、関西の美術館、博物館、資料館などの入館料（原則として常設展）を11月に無料とする取り組みです。今年は、11月14日（土）〜15日（日）を中心日として開催されます。

福井県、三重県、滋賀県、京都府、大阪府、兵庫県、奈良県、和歌山県、鳥取県、徳島県の2府8県の文化施設のうち、450以上の施設が参加！（通年にわたって入館無料の施設も参加対象）

参加施設は 公式HP でも確認できますが、「多すぎて選べない！」という方に向けて、入館無料となる施設の一部を紹介します。

…レベルだと、「場所だけは貸すが一切関与しない」ということはままあり得ます。ただ、この映画は時代劇アクションもので上記のような論点はなく、確かに「画像飛び」があることは確認してはいますが、シアターセブンさん等では通常起こるレベルの、初監督やそれに準じる方の作品では起きる「許容範囲内」の話ではあります。 一方、貸館上映のことをどちらが持ちかけたかは不明ですが（監督さんサイドの可能性もある）、その場合でも、映画館は１人でも多く入ってもらわないと成り立たない形態です。また、一人でも客がいる（予約者がいる）以上、上映費は固定費として発生しますが、変動費であるチケット代は何人入るかで異なります。つまり、どうであろうがシアターセブンさん側に少なくとも、劇場側が簡単な告知を行うことに大きな障害があったとは考えにくいわけです。もちろんこのことが、「余りにも内容が不愉快すぎる」といった事情であれば別ですが、何度も書いているように時代劇アクションものです。 YAMANEKO

解説・あらすじ

激動の幕末を舞台に、言葉を失った異国の少女と、言葉を話さず山奥に隠れ住む謎の男の出会いと数奇な運命を描いたアクション時代劇。「ウルトラマン」シリーズのスーツアクターをはじめ、スタントマンやアクション俳優として活動する丸山貢治が主演・監督・脚本を手がけ、自身の主宰する劇団丸組で上演した舞台「山猫」を映画版として生まれ変わらせた。丸山監督が自らアクション監督も務め、現代的なアレンジを加えた殺陣や素手のファイトを用いたアクションシーンを散りばめて描き出す。 目の前で母親を殺されたショックで言葉を失った異国の少女クレア。薩摩藩から逃れ京都に辿り着いた彼女は、鞍馬山の奥深くにたったひとりで生きる、言葉を話さない謎の男・山猫と出会う。言葉を交わさなくともクレアを守る山猫だったが、そんな2人の前に立ちはだかったのは薩摩藩の追手ではなく、幕府が送り込んだ新選組だった。 言葉を失った少女クレアを「小さな恋のうた」「翔んで埼玉 琵琶湖より愛をこめて」のトミコ・クレア、謎の男・山猫を丸山貢治が演じ、特撮ドラマ「ウルトラマントリガー」シリーズの豊田ルナが共演。
